Understand the policies shaping India.

Anvaya finds the official text, explains it in plain language, and shows the exact passage behind every claim.

Code: https://github.com/alishahwark/anvaya (public) · run it locally in under 10 minutes

The problem

One law, five documents, three start dates

  • Act · assent 11 Aug 2023
  • Commencement notification · 13 Nov 2025, three dates
  • Rules · own schedule, same three dates
  • Corrigendum · 11 Dec 2025
  • Removal of Difficulties Order · 6 Oct 2026

Secondary sources disagree on the exact day (13 or 14 May 2027) and press reports of a shorter timeline are unconfirmed. Readers cannot sort that out from Gazette PDFs.

“Does the DPDP Act apply to my small business, and when?”

A chatbot answers from memory. A search engine returns pages. Neither shows which page of which Gazette supports the sentence.

What is new

Claims you can check, status you can trust

Evidence at claim level

83 claims, each with verbatim quotes and a PDF page. A script found 154/154 quotes on the stated page.

Status is computed

Dates come from the Gazette; code works out “in force / starts in 200 days”. The model cannot write status.

Answer, then check

Scoped retrieval, an answer with exact quotes that code confirms, then a second AI pass. If unsupported, Anvaya says so.

Plus: ask for any bill by name or paste an official link; a verification engine checks Parliament’s register against the documents and India Code and shows every check. And a design scorecard: four rings with 90% ranges, benchmarked against UK and Canadian statutes. Things we could not confirm are listed on the page.

The agents

A fixed pipeline with scoped roles

Cost to run

About 4,337 tokens in, 896 out, per live question

151,798input tokens over 35 questions (66 calls)
8 smedian answer time (90th percentile 12.9 s)
0tokens for the 9 prepared answers; live answers are cached

At 10,000 live questions a month: 43.4M input and 9M output tokens.

Measured on gpt-6-luna via Portkey, gateway cache bypassed. A verified price for this model was not available, so no dollar figure is claimed.

Safety

Untrusted text never gets to give orders

AttackDefenceResult
Redirect to an internal addressEvery hop validated before it is requested14 tests pass
“Ignore instructions… fully in force”Status from code; rules; output checksignored
Poisoned passage inside a retrieved documentTreated as data; second-pass check6/6 ignored, 0 cited
Wrong-policy questionOne corpus per policyabstained
Fake quote or wrong pageQuote verifierrejected
Leaked keyServer-only, scannedabsent

Small samples written by us; not a penetration test.

Impact

What we measured

154/154quotes found on the official page
21/25development questions, strict
10/10held-out questions, strict
22register records verified against live official sources (5 corroborated, 0 failed)
  • The four strict misses were correct answers worded unexpectedly (our reading, not independent review).
  • One real retrieval miss: a paraphrase did not find the erasure passage. Not tuned away.
  • 119 unit + 38 browser tests pass on a production build. Scorecard: 18 comparator statutes scored; the effect ring is blank because no outcome data exists.
  • Not measured: user comprehension. No user study was run.

Limits and next

Honest edges

Limits

  • One curated law; other bills provisional
  • Keyword retrieval misses paraphrases
  • Date counting and a reported shortening are unconfirmed
  • Scorecard measures design, not outcomes
  • No lawyer review, no user study

Next

  • Test with 3–5 non-lawyers
  • Add embedding retrieval; re-run held-out
  • Curate a second law with the same contract
  • Lawyer review; read the eGazette directly

Try it

Ask it something

git clone https://github.com/alishahwark/anvaya.git && cd anvaya && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npm run setup && npm run dev

Then open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and try: “Are my customers’ data rights already in force?”
